To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the basal and norepiinephrine-stimulated production of inosltol monophosphates are greater in the atria of DOCA-salted hypertensive rats than in normotensive rats, but that the α1-adrenergeic receptors of these rats are unchanged or even decreased.

DOCA-salt hypertension is associated with an increased activity of the phosphatidyl inositol pathway in cardiovascular tissues, as suggested by an increased production of inositoh monophosphate in atria, ventricle, and femoral arteries.

the production of ino-sitol monophosphate, an index of phosphoinositide metabolism, was found to he greater in cardiovascular tissues of rats treated with deoxycortico-sterone acetate (DOGA) and 1 % saline (DOCA-salt) for 4 weeks compared with normotenslvie rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of α1-adrenoreceptor-mediated inositol phospholipid metabolism in cardiovascular tissues of hypertensive rats.
the study of the phosphatidyl-inositol turnover as a mechanism for the control of the contractile state of the heart.
the effects of chronic hypertension on the phosphoinositid pathway in rat heart and femoral artery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the DOCA-salt model of hypertension, in addition to the well-known increase of vascular resistance, is characterized by increased activity and sensitivity of α1-adrenoreceptors and phosphatidylinositide pathway.
the phosphoinositidc pathway is involved in the pathogenesis of experimental hypertension.

α1-adrenergc receptors are not involved in the pathogenesis of DOCA-salr-induced hypertension, but that the increased activity of the phosphatidylino-sitold pathway in the heart of these hypertensive rats may be responsible for the cardiac hypertrophy and for the increased cardiac output.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phosphatidylnositide pathway plays an important role in mediating the effects of the increased sympathoadrenal activity in DOCA-salted hypertensive rats.

the increased inositol monphosphate production in cardiovascular tissue of DOCA salt hypertensive rats may be due to an increased sensitivity of α-adrenergic or β-adrenergic stimulation of inositol phospholipase C.

the increased inositol monophsphate production in cardiovascular tissues is associated with a hypersensitivity of the phosphatidyl inositol pathway and/or a hypersensitivity of α1-adrenoreceptors in DOCA-sal hypertensive rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we found an increased production of inositoi monophosphate in cardiovascular tissues of hypertensive rats.
the inositol monositol phosphate pathway is a key regulator of the cardiovascular system.
the use of the inositol monosphosphate accumulation assay is an excellent way to study the phosphatidyinositol pathway.
